A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SOE research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: V1 reports original mathematical benchmark evaluations, rank-decay measurements, probe-selection ablations, and experiments across three random seeds in Section 5 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds PRM comparisons, control experiments, larger-model evaluations, threshold sensitivity, and logic/code benchmark results.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain greedy-trace truncation, Monte Carlo manifold estimation, Micro-SVD, eight-token Student probes, orthogonal-residual maximization, and Teacher continuation. Equations 3–7 preserve the same procedure; revised terminology and deployment do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates mathematical reasoning only. V2 retains the five mathematical benchmarks and adds actual evaluations on ZebraLogic and HumanEvalPlus (Section 5.5/Table 7), substantially extending coverage to logic puzzles and code generation.

E2.justification: V1 compares against Self-Consistency and a random-probe ablation. V2 retains both and adds PRM-guided, step-level Best-of-N comparisons on AIME 2024, AIME 2025, and MATH-500 (Table 4). This materially expands the comparator set to reward-guided step selection.

E3.justification: The original difficult-subset Pass@16 protocol remains. V2 adds Qwen3-8B/32B Teachers, alternative 7B Students, matched sampling positions and continuation counts for PRM comparisons, and controls using 16 trajectories per problem with first/last 500-token measurements. Latency evaluation changes from Hugging Face generation to vLLM, and Table 6 introduces normalization by 1.128.

E4.justification: V2 adds controls contrasting short/long and correct/incorrect traces to examine verbosity confounding (Table 5), diversity-threshold sensitivity from 0.80 to 1.00 (Appendix C.3/Table 9), and wall-clock-normalized efficiency analysis (Table 6). The original random-probe ablation and orthogonality distribution are retained.

E5.justification: The three AIME 2025 seeds, 42, 1024, and 2024, and their reporting remain unchanged (v1 Table 4; v2 Table 10). Existing shaded plots are retained. V2 introduces no new uncertainty estimation, significance testing, or repeated-run reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original benchmark, ablation, seed, and exploration-curve results remain unchanged, but v2 adds extensive results for the new comparisons and analyses. Table 7 reports baseline/SOE accuracies of 56.23%/58.72% on ZebraLogic and 10.00%/16.67% on HumanEvalPlus. The 2.60-second Hugging Face latency is replaced by a 0.46-second vLLM measurement under different deployment conditions.

T1.justification: V1's Theorem 2 claims exponential spectral decay; v2's Proposition 2 and Appendix D.2 narrow this to rank non-expansion and revise the attention-concentration argument. Section 6.3 removes the infinite-SNR argument and replaces unconditional rank augmentation by a nondecrease statement plus an idealized rank-plus-one case. Appendix D.1 also qualifies the nonlinear-layer argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace categorical geometric-collapse and knowledge-exclusion claims with associations and partly geometric explanations. V2 also claims preliminary effectiveness on logic and code generation. The headline 62.4% accuracy and 113.7% sampling-efficiency improvements remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 and Appendix D.3 introduce attention rerouting by semantically structured probes as a hypothesis and allow informational contributions. V2 explicitly states that rank augmentation does not guarantee better reasoning and interprets the new controls as evidence beyond verbosity. Section 8 revises generalization limitations to acknowledge larger-model and nonmathematical evaluations.

D1.justification: V2 documents optimized vLLM deployment, revised component timings, and approximately 3.6 seconds of end-to-end inference per problem. The advertised repository path changes from SOE- to spectral-orthogonal-exploration. Core probe and sampling hyperparameters remain, while the added experiments receive limited implementation detail.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Jiang et al. (2023) for Mistral 7B, Lin et al. (2025) for ZebraLogic, and Liu et al. (2023) for code evaluation. The principal related-work discussion and positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, motivation, method exposition, theoretical discussion, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting, with more qualified language and orthogonal-complement terminology. Section 6 is retitled, experimental and appendix subsections are expanded or reorganized, and author/affiliation information changes.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 4 are substantially redrawn, Figure 1 changes its null-space label, and Figure 6 revises its categories and axis for vLLM timings. Six new tables display added experiments. The orthogonality distribution moves from main-text Figure 7 to appendix Figure 10, with corresponding layout and numbering changes.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's limited comparison/control evidence and overstrong theoretical guarantees. PRM comparisons, verbosity controls, threshold sensitivity, and broader model/task evaluations strengthen empirical support, while Section 6 and Appendix D narrow conclusions to better match the arguments. New experimental details remain sparse, and Table 6 uses arithmetic runtime normalization rather than a matched-time rerun, but the overall gains in evidential support and claim calibration are substantial.
